stories.head: US lifts nationwide flight ground stop after air traffic communications failure
stories.say: America's aviation regulator halted departing flights nationwide on Friday after a communications failure hit air traffic control, before lifting the stop that night.
stories.stand: Thousands of flights were cancelled or delayed in the first nationwide ground stop since January 2023.
body: The US Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop for departing flights on Friday afternoon, citing extraordinary circumstances and safety. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue had hit all air route traffic control centres.

Al Jazeera said the stop began at 3:54pm Eastern Time. Yahoo News reported it was lifted on Friday night. By 6:45pm Eastern, FlightAware counted more than 10,000 delayed and more than 3,200 cancelled flights in, into or out of the US, Yahoo said.

Duffy blamed instability in radar communications and an old air traffic system. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said it did not appear to be a cyber attack. Microsoft said its own global outage did not appear to be a factor.
It was the first nationwide ground stop since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system failed, Al Jazeera reported. Congress approved $12.5bn last year to overhaul the system.

stories.head: Five countries picked to speak for Europe in Ukraine peace talks
stories.say: European leaders meeting in Dublin on Friday named Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland to represent Europe in the next round of Ukraine peace talks, rejecting a single envoy.
stories.stand: The EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas had sought the role of single envoy but was left out.
body: EU leaders agreed on Friday that the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Poland will represent Europe at the next round of US-brokered talks on ending the war in Ukraine. European Council President António Costa announced the team in Dublin.

The European Council, the European Commission and NATO will also be represented, Euronews reported. Leaders declined to appoint a single envoy, despite calls for one, including from Italy's prime minister Giorgia Meloni.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas had publicly sought the role. She said the Russians did not want her. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner said after meeting Vladimir Putin on Thursday that Europe would join future talks, but the Kremlin said no decision had been made.

stories.head: Tanker hits docked river cruise boat in New Orleans
stories.say: A tanker struck the docked riverboat American Heritage in New Orleans on Friday, leaving it partly submerged with about 129 passengers on board, port officials said.
stories.stand: Several people were rescued from the Mississippi as the paddlewheel boat listed into the water.
body: A tanker collided with the paddlewheel riverboat American Heritage in New Orleans on Friday, leaving it partly submerged, Euronews and ABC News reported. ABC named the tanker as the Atlantic Asphalt.
The Port of New Orleans said about 129 passengers were on board. Video showed the riverboat being hit while it appeared to be docked.

The office of Mayor Helena Moreno said several people had been rescued and that search and rescue work was continuing. Passengers were taken to the port's administration building. There was no official information on injuries.

stories.head: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it destroyed a US radar in Bahrain
stories.say: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said on Friday it destroyed an American early-warning radar in Bahrain, in response to a strike on a telecoms tower in southern Iran. The claim was not verified.
stories.stand: It was Iran's first reported targeting of a facility in Bahrain since September.
body: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said on Friday its forces had destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain, Iranian state media reported. Bahrain hosts the headquarters of the US Navy's Fifth Fleet.

The Guard said it acted after an attack on a telecommunications tower in Sirik county in southern Iran on Thursday. It called its strike a serious warning to Washington. The claim could not be independently verified, ITV News reported.
The Guard also said a liquefied gas tanker struck a mine and exploded in the Strait of Hormuz. The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency had no immediate report of that incident.

stories.say: Türkiye and Qatar signed a mutual defence agreement in Istanbul on Friday, after talks between President Erdogan and the Emir of Qatar.
stories.stand: President Erdogan said the two countries would work to prevent a renewed war in the Gulf.
body: Türkiye and Qatar signed a mutual defence agreement in Istanbul on Friday after a meeting between President Tayyip Erdogan and Qatar's Emir, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, Al Jazeera reported.

Erdogan's office said the deal would add a new dimension to relations. Several other agreements were signed, including one on co-operation in conflict resolution. The text of the defence pact was not published.
Turkish troops are already based in Qatar. In August, Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed a regional defence pact, which Türkiye's parliament ratified last week.

stories.head: Paraguay's ex-president Peña faces new charge over Ueno bank collapse
stories.say: Prosecutors in Paraguay charged former president Santiago Peña with criminal association on Friday over the collapse of the digital bank Ueno. He denies all charges.
stories.stand: The charge came a week after Congress removed Peña from office by impeachment.
body: Paraguayan prosecutors charged former president Santiago Peña with criminal association on Friday over the collapse of the digital bank Ueno, Al Jazeera reported. He already faced charges of breach of trust and self-dealing, and denies them all.
Prosecutors allege Peña steered government funds to the bank and played down its problems. Ueno held more than $800m in public funds. Peña is in pre-trial detention at a military facility.
Three former central bank officials were arrested on Friday. The central bank said it had returned savings to more than 1.8 million depositors.

stories.head: Nigeria finishes Ebola contact checks with no further cases
stories.say: Nigeria says all 62 contacts of its first Ebola patient in more than a decade have completed 21 days of monitoring without falling ill.
stories.stand: Health officials said the outbreak cannot yet be declared over under WHO rules.
body: Nigeria's Centre for Disease Control and Prevention said 62 contacts of an Ebola patient finished 21 days of monitoring without falling ill, Al Jazeera reported. 13 had symptoms but all tested negative.
Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case in more than a decade on 20 October. The patient, who had travelled from Uganda, was evacuated to Switzerland and has recovered.

The agency said a full 42-day countdown is needed before the outbreak can be declared over. The outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has infected more than 11,000 people, according to government data.

stories.head: Brooklyn building collapse killed eight, including two children
stories.say: Eight people, two of them children, died when a three-storey building collapsed in Brooklyn on Wednesday, New York's mayor Zohran Mamdani said.
stories.stand: Construction work was under way next door; the cause has not been determined.
body: A three-storey apartment building in Brooklyn collapsed on Wednesday afternoon while workers dug at a neighbouring lot, ITV News reported. Mayor Zohran Mamdani said eight people died, two children aged nine and 10 and six adults.
Eighteen people were injured, including four firefighters. Rescue work ended on Thursday.
The cause has not been determined. Mamdani ordered inspections of about 100 sites linked to companies involved in the project. A stop-work order was issued at the site in March, ITV reported.

stories.head: Rival armed groups fight each other in northern Burkina Faso
stories.say: Al-Qaeda and Islamic State affiliates are fighting each other along Burkina Faso's border with Mali, with ACLED recording more than 2,200 fighters killed in their clashes.
stories.stand: The state is struggling to reassert control over large parts of the country, Al Jazeera reports.
body: The al-Qaeda affiliate JNIM and the Islamic State's Sahel Province are fighting for territory along Burkina Faso's northern border with Mali, Al Jazeera reported.

The monitoring group ACLED has recorded about 320 clashes between them and more than 2,200 fighter deaths. Islamic State claimed in October that it killed more than 400 JNIM fighters; that claim has not been independently confirmed.
The UN says about 4.5 million people in Burkina Faso need humanitarian aid this year.

stories.stand: Washington imposed sanctions on Myanmar's military after the 2021 coup.
body: Senior Trump administration officials have held talks with Myanmar's government, led by coup leader turned president Min Aung Hlaing, ABC News reported. The most recent meeting was in Tokyo in October.

A State Department document cited by ABC named access to Myanmar's rare earth resources as a possible goal, alongside countering China's influence. China controls about 90% of global rare earth production, an analyst told ABC.
The US imposed sanctions and cut ties after the February 2021 coup. Rights campaigners criticised the talks.

stories.say: Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot on Friday accused Benjamin Netanyahu of fuelling a racist campaign against Palestinian citizens of Israel.
stories.stand: Neither bloc won a majority in the 27 October election, and coalition talks continue.
body: Gadi Eisenkot, who is trying to form Israel's next government, accused caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday of fuelling a racist and violent campaign against Palestinian citizens of Israel, Al Jazeera reported. He posted the statement on X.
In the 27 October election, Eisenkot's four-party alliance won 48 seats and Netanyahu's bloc won 53; 61 are needed for a majority. Arab-led parties won a record 19 seats.
Electoral authorities rejected fraud allegations Netanyahu made against Arab-majority parties. Eisenkot has six weeks to form a government.

stories.head: Russian business delegation visits Kabul for talks with the Taliban
stories.say: Russia's deputy prime minister Alexei Overchuk took a delegation of 70 business people to Kabul for talks with Taliban leaders on trade and investment.
stories.stand: Russia is the only country to have formally recognised the Taliban government.
body: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexei Overchuk led a delegation of 70 business people to Kabul on Thursday, Euronews reported. They met Taliban leaders including Prime Minister Mohammad Hassan Akhund.

Overchuk said Afghanistan was interested in Russian fertilisers and in building fertiliser plants. He said trade between the two countries more than doubled in the first eight months of 2026, to over $349m. No deals were reported signed.
Russia recognised the Taliban government in July 2025, the only country to do so since the group took power in 2021.

stories.say: A Russian overnight strike set fire to a medical facility in Kyiv, and a drone attack killed one person in Odesa, Ukrainian officials said on Friday.
stories.stand: Patients including wheelchair users were helped out as the fire spread to the second floor.
body: A Russian overnight strike hit a medical facility in Kyiv's Shevchenkivskyi district, starting a fire that partly destroyed its second floor, Ukraine's State Emergency Service said, according to Euronews.
Staff evacuated 30 people and rescuers saved another seven. The fire was brought under control.
In Odesa, a Russian drone attack killed one person and injured others, said Serhii Lysak, head of the city's military administration.

stories.say: Some Iranian MPs are pressing to leave the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty and change the country's nuclear doctrine, though Iran's foreign ministry says it remains committed to the treaty.
stories.stand: A bill to withdraw from the treaty has not reached a vote.
body: Some Iranian MPs are calling for Iran to review its nuclear doctrine and leave the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, Euronews reported. MP Kamran Ghazanfari told Euronews that building nuclear weapons was essential for Iran.
A bill to withdraw from the treaty has not reached the floor of parliament. On Thursday, the Assembly of Experts called for withdrawal to be examined.
Iran's foreign ministry has said the country remains committed to the treaty. A former MP, Heshmatollah Falahatpisheh, told Euronews that leaving would lay the ground for future wars.

stories.say: South Africa's ANC says President Cyril Ramaphosa will not step down, after the party's vote fell to 31 percent in local elections, its worst result.
stories.stand: The party will now negotiate coalitions in councils where no one won a majority.
body: South Africa's governing ANC said on Thursday that President Cyril Ramaphosa will not resign, Africanews reported. Spokesperson Mahlengi Bhengu-Motsiri dismissed reports that he had offered to step down as fabrication.
The party's vote share fell 15 percentage points to 31% in this month's local elections, its worst result. It lost its national majority in 2024.
The ANC's secretary-general called the result catastrophic. The party will negotiate coalitions in councils where no party won a majority.

stories.say: The new head of the World Food Programme, Luke Lindberg, has called for an end to Sudan's war, saying funding shortfalls left 900,000 people without food aid.
stories.stand: The UN says about 34 million people in Sudan need humanitarian help.
body: Luke J. Lindberg, the new executive director of the UN World Food Programme, called for an end to the fighting in Sudan during a visit to a camp for displaced people, Africanews reported.
The WFP fed 4 million people in Sudan in August, but funding shortfalls forced cuts that left 900,000 without help. It is seeking $520m to feed 5.4 million people until April 2027.
The UN says about 34 million people, nearly two-thirds of Sudan's population, need humanitarian assistance.

stories.head: Two Iranian men found guilty of spying on London journalists for Iran
stories.say: Two Iranian men were found guilty on Thursday of spying for Iran's intelligence service on two Iran International journalists and a lawyer in London, intending violence against them.
stories.stand: A third man was cleared of all charges; sentencing is set for 17 December.
body: Mostafa Sepahvand, 41, and Farhad Javadi Manesh, 46, were found guilty at Woolwich Crown Court on Thursday after a six-week trial, Al Jazeera reported. They were convicted of conduct likely to assist Iran's intelligence service, with intent to inflict violence on people in the UK.

The targets were two journalists from Iran International, a Persian-language broadcaster in London, and Jonathan Turner, a founder of UK Lawyers for Israel. The court heard the men visited addresses linked to them and took photographs and videos.

A third man, Shapoor Qalehali Khani Noori, 57, was acquitted. The Metropolitan Police said it was the fourth case in recent years involving direct threats to Iranian journalists in the UK. Sentencing is due on 17 December at the Old Bailey.

stories.say: Wessex Water pleaded guilty on Friday to three health and safety offences over the December 2020 explosion at its Avonmouth site in Bristol, which killed four workers.
stories.stand: The case has been sent to Bristol Crown Court for sentencing in January.
body: Wessex Water pleaded guilty at Bristol Magistrates' Court to three offences under the Health and Safety at Work Act, Yahoo News reported, carrying a BBC report.
The charges relate to an explosion in a silo at its Avonmouth treatment site in December 2020. Four workers died, including a teenage apprentice.

The judge sent the case to Bristol Crown Court, with sentencing set for 8 January. A police manslaughter investigation was dropped in 2024, and the Health and Safety Executive brought the charges this year.

stories.head: More than 80,000 knives taken off the streets since July 2024, Home Office says
stories.say: The Home Office says 80,190 knives and other weapons have been seized or handed in since July 2024, and knife crime in England and Wales is down 11 percent since the election.
stories.stand: Ministers say they want to halve knife crime within a decade.
body: The Home Office said on Friday that 80,190 knives and weapons have been removed or seized since July 2024, about 100 a day. The figure includes 47,795 zombie-style knives and machetes handed in under a surrender scheme.
It said knife crime in England and Wales is down 11% since the general election, and knife-enabled robbery is down 24% across the seven most affected police forces.
Policing Minister Sarah Jones said the government could not be satisfied while lives were still being lost. The government aims to halve knife crime within 10 years.

stories.say: Two Northern Ireland police officers have been dismissed for secretly recording vulnerable people while on duty, in conduct the Police Ombudsman called utterly despicable.
stories.stand: One officer recorded or photographed 18 vulnerable people between 2016 and 2021, the ombudsman found.
body: Two Police Service of Northern Ireland officers have been dismissed after recording vulnerable people while on duty, ITV News reported. A third received a final written warning.

The Police Ombudsman found one officer recorded or photographed 18 vulnerable people, including people who had asked for help, and shared images on WhatsApp. The investigation also found 74 officers had accessed body-worn video without a legitimate reason.
Ombudsman Jacqui Durkin called the behaviour utterly despicable. Deputy Chief Constable Bobby Singleton described it as horrifying.

stories.stand: Brand has not officially responded to the new claims, which have not been tested in court.

The allegations, which have not been tested in court, include sex without consent. Some date back to 2015, ABC said.
Brand was recently found guilty at Southwark Crown Court of one count of rape and three of sexual assault against four women between 2004 and 2009. He was jailed for more than 10 years.

The biggest rise was in Portugal, at 60.8%, followed by the Netherlands at 34.3% and Hungary at 26.5%. Spain rose 24.5%.
The ratio fell most in Romania, by 42.8%, and in Finland, by 25.2%. EU house prices rose 62% in the 10 years to the second quarter of 2026.

stories.stand: The carbon could have formed through biology or ordinary chemistry; returned samples would be needed to tell.
body: NASA's Perseverance rover has confirmed macromolecular carbon, large networks of carbon atoms, in two ancient rocks in the Bright Angel formation of Jezero Crater, ScienceDaily reported. The study is published in Science Advances.
The rover's SHERLOC instrument detected the carbon using laser light. It survived only a few microns below the rock surface, the shallowest such detection reported on Mars.

body: Mangroves lost nearly 3,000 sq km between 1984 and 2010 but gained nearly 2,000 sq km after 2010, according to a study in Science using Landsat images, NASA's Earth Observatory reported.

stories.head: New Zealand thrash India by 244 runs as Henry takes six
stories.say: New Zealand beat India by 244 runs in the fourth one-day international, bowling them out for 89 after Matt Henry took three wickets in the first over.
stories.stand: India still lead the series 2-1 with one match left.
body: New Zealand beat India by 244 runs in the fourth one-day international at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui, on Friday, Al Jazeera reported. New Zealand made 333 and bowled India out for 89.
Matt Henry took 6-27, dismissing Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer without scoring in the first over of the chase. Will Young made 125 off 108 balls.
India lead the five-match series 2-1. The final match is at the same ground on Sunday.

stories.stand: Australia lead the three-match series 1-0, with the second game in Adelaide on Sunday.
body: Australia beat England by seven wickets in the first one-day international in Perth on Friday, Dawn reported. England were bowled out for 131 in 33.4 overs.

stories.head: Pat Cummins calls Khawaja's sandpaper claims 'utter nonsense'
stories.say: Australia captain Pat Cummins has rejected Usman Khawaja's claim that all the players knew about the 2018 ball-tampering plot, calling it utter nonsense.
stories.stand: Khawaja made the claims in an autobiography published on Tuesday.
body: Australia captain Pat Cummins told a news conference in Sydney on Friday that Usman Khawaja's claims about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal were utter nonsense, Al Jazeera reported.
In an autobiography published on Tuesday, Khawaja said all the players knew about the plan to rough up the ball with sandpaper in South Africa. Cummins said he was 100% wrong.
David Warner said he stood by Khawaja's account. Cricket Australia's chief ruled out a new investigation earlier in the week.

stories.stand: Pegula faces Mirra Andreeva in the semi-finals on Saturday.
body: Jessica Pegula beat Linda Noskova 7-6 (7/2), 4-6, 7-5 in her final group match at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells on Thursday, saving a match point, Al Jazeera reported.
The result sent Pegula through and eliminated Coco Gauff, who had earlier beaten Marta Kostyuk 6-4, 7-5.
The tournament was moved from Riyadh because of the US-Israel war on Iran. Pegula plays Mirra Andreeva in the semi-finals on Saturday.

stories.say: England beat France 50-38 in Wollongong on Friday to win the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup for the third time.
stories.stand: Joe Coyd scored four tries and Jack Brown a hat-trick.
body: England beat France 50-38 in the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup final in Wollongong, Australia, on Friday, ABC News reported. It is England's third world title.
Joe Coyd scored four tries and Jack Brown finished with a hat-trick, including a try just before half-time from a Rob Hawkins kick.
England and France have won all five World Cups between them.

stories.head: FIA bans Daily Mail's F1 reporter over Leclerc column
stories.say: Formula One's governing body has withdrawn the media pass of the Daily Mail's motor racing correspondent Jonathan McEvoy for the rest of the season, over a column about Charles Leclerc.
stories.stand: The Daily Mail called the ban an outrageous attack on press freedom.
body: The FIA has withdrawn the accreditation of Jonathan McEvoy, the Daily Mail's motor racing correspondent, for the rest of the 2026 season, AOL reported, carrying a Telegraph story.

The ban followed an opinion piece using an insult about Ferrari's Charles Leclerc over his conduct after the Mexico City Grand Prix. The FIA said the article fell short of the standards expected of accredited media.
The Daily Mail's head of sport, Chris Dean, called the ban an unprecedented and outrageous attack on the freedom of the press.

stories.say: Carter Gordon returns at fly-half for Australia against Scotland at Murrayfield on Sunday, two months after breaking his leg, as the Wallabies try to end a run of heavy defeats.
stories.stand: Australia lost 45-22 to England last weekend, their third heavy defeat in a row.
body: Carter Gordon returns at fly-half for Australia's Test against Scotland at Murrayfield on Sunday, two months after breaking his leg against Argentina, ABC News reported. Declan Meredith drops out.
Coach Les Kiss moves Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to inside centre, and Rob Valetini returns at number six.
Australia lost 45-22 to England at Twickenham, their third heavy defeat in a row.
